name: Atlas
oneLiner: Reach as cartography: a contour map with your cause at the summit and supporters pinned around it.
concept:
Nonprofit Megaphone's job, stripped of jargon, is to put a cause in front of the people already searching for it. Atlas makes that literal. The hero is a topographic map drawn in inline SVG: real marching-squares contours over a summit and three knolls, the nonprofit's coral pin at the summit with its $10,000 a month Google Ad Grant on the label, and smaller pins on the surrounding hills where supporters were found, each carrying a sample twelve-month outcome from the case files (2,300 new visitors a month; 300+ screenings a month; $38,000 a month in donations) and a SAMPLE tag rather than a client name. The lowest, dashed contour is Google's 5% click-through floor: keep the account above it or the grant is lost. Everything on the sheet behaves like a map, not a dashboard: a neatline with graticule ticks and grid numbers, a compass rose, 'Sheet 01 · Reach survey', an 'As of 22 Sep 2026' readout in mono, a three-row legend, and twelve stepped hypsometric tints that lighten toward the summit. The geometry is one aria-hidden SVG; every label is real DOM text, and a hidden figcaption states the whole argument.

The register is expedition-grade: precise, calm, unhurried. A pale steel blue-gray ground (the only cool ground in the set), contour lines in muted blue, deep navy ink, and one coral for pins and the CTA, a deliberate continuity with the button colour on the current site. Because white on that coral fails AA (3.4:1), buttons carry navy text (4.78:1) and coral is never used as type, which is what keeps a warm accent from tipping a cool page into alarm. Type is Source Serif 4 for display and letterspaced small caps, Source Sans 3 for body and UI, DM Mono for dates and grid references styled like survey readouts. The trust strip is built from map furniture too: the Letter from Google as an attestation stamp with Michelle Hurtado named, the three trust figures set as the divisions of a scale bar captioned 'Scale of operations · as of Sep 2026', and the client roll as an index in small caps. On the phone the map folds to a small inset sheet with numbered markers and a keyed list, so every figure stays readable text.
distinctFrom: It is the only direction on a cool steel-blue ground and the only one whose signature is a place (a contour map with pins) rather than a signal, a ledger, a civic form, a poster or a signed letter.
bullets: Contour-map hero: your cause at the summit, supporters pinned around it.
Steel-blue ground, navy ink, one coral for pins and the CTA.
Map furniture carries trust: scale-bar figures, dated readouts, a legend.
rightFor: A leadership team that wants calm, forwardable authority and one memorable idea, and will keep the map disciplined rather than decorative.
needs: Approve coral buttons with navy text
Decide whether client cities get plotted

palette.note: Pale steel blue-gray page ground, the only cool ground in the set, and the lowest hypsometric tint. Contour fills step from it to #F9FBFC at the summit in twelve flat increments computed from the terrain, never a gradient. Also the backing behind the sheet label and the floor label, which cross only the dashed floor line (the fill on both sides of that line is the ground, so the backing never shows as a patch).

Pin label cards, the legend, the 'As of 22 Sep 2026' date plate (it sits over the hypsometric tints, where a ground backing would read as a patch), the Letter from Google stamp, the compass face and the scale bar's light segments. 1px #C9D5DE hairline, 3px radius, no shadow; a 10px navy leader ties each card to its pin.

Deep navy for headlines, nav, the neatline and seam, compass, pin outlines, the dashed 5% floor, the scale bar's dark segments and CTA text. 13.7:1 on ground, 16.2:1 on white, 4.78:1 on the coral button. Body copy uses #2E3D57 (9.2:1 on ground).
Small caps labels, mono readouts, graticule numbers, card sub-lines, figure labels. 5.4:1 on ground, 6.4:1 on white, 6.1:1 on the summit tint; the floor colour for any 11px text.
Card edges, the trust strip's inner rules, the client roll's dividers, the SAMPLE and 2 MIN tag borders, the portrait frame. #DEE6EC for rules inside white cards.
Contour lines only: 1px regular, 1.5px index every fourth line, round joins. 1.8:1 on ground by design so it reads as terrain and never competes with text; never used for type or UI.

The single accent: pin heads, the compass's north point, the eyebrow pin and the CTA fill; continuity with the current site's coral button. Never text: 2.9:1 on ground fails even large-text AA, so pins carry a 0.8px navy hairline and buttons carry navy text. Hover #EC7A55 (navy text 5.8:1); pressed state adds a navy border instead of darkening.
The top hypsometric step. The summit reads brighter so the main pin and its card sit on the lightest ground; the steps between it and the page ground are generated with the contours, not hand-picked.

typography.display: Source Serif 4 (Google Fonts, variable, optical size 8-60): 600 at display optical size for h1 (58px desktop, 40px phone), the 26px scale-bar figures, the 16px summit card title and the 17px wordmark; 400 italic for the Letter from Google quote (20px desktop, 19px phone). Letterspaced small caps (font-variant-caps: all-small-caps, 0.14em, 13px, weight 600) for every label that names a thing: eyebrow, sheet label, stamp, 'Get a free quote', the roll label, and the client roll itself at 15px / 0.08em.
typography.body: Source Sans 3 (Google Fonts): 400 body (18px hero sub on desktop, 16px phone), 500 nav links, 600 buttons, pin card titles (14px), the phone key (14px) and the guarantee line's lead (15px). All three families load from fonts.googleapis.com only; no Fontshare, no self-hosted fonts.
typography.mono: DM Mono (Google Fonts): 400/500 at 11px uppercase, 0.08em, for every readout: 'As of 22 Sep 2026', grid references ('Summit · grid 43 · 71'), graticule numbers, the SAMPLE tag, the 15 MIN / 2 MIN tags, fine print, the wordmark sub-line, figure labels (tracked 0.04em) and 'Scale of operations'. Dates are styled like survey readouts, never as sentences.
typography.scaleNotes: Desktop h1 58px / 1.02 / -0.015em, sentence case, held to two lines ('Put your cause' / 'on the map.') at max-width 464px; no colour in the headline because coral is never type. Phone h1 40px / 1.02. Sub 18px / 1.5 at max-width 452px, 16px on the phone. Card titles 14px Source Sans 600; card sub-lines, tags and every readout 11px DM Mono, the floor across the system (nothing is set smaller). Small caps labels are set at 13px so their small-cap glyphs sit near the cap height of 11px mono. Buttons 52px (40px in the nav, 36px in the phone nav), 15-16px Source Sans 600, 4px radius, with an 11px mono time tag. Trust figures 26px Source Serif 600 over 11px mono labels. Spacing on an 8px base: nav 72, hero 600, trust 153 (frame 825px); phone nav 60, inset 178, key rows 30, CTA top 613, eligibility 675. Uppercase is reserved for mono readouts, small caps for serif labels, headings are sentence case. Every figure carries a unit and a date ('$48M+ · as of Sep 2026') as a CMS rule.

layout:
- Grid: 12 columns, 1200px container, 48px gutters at desktop, 24px tablet, 16px phone; vertical rhythm on 8px. Sections are separated by 1px navy rules that read as neatlines, each opened by a small caps sheet label ('Sheet 02 · The rules') instead of numbered mono. The map token set (contours, pin, card, legend, compass, scale bar) appears at most three times per page: hero, outcomes atlas, reporting sheet. Every map ships as static inline SVG generated once per breakpoint.
- 00 Nav (72px, navy rule beneath acting as the neatline, graticule ticks running under it across the map column): navy circular mark + 'Nonprofit Megaphone' in Source Serif 600 with an 11px mono sub-line; Services, Our work, Happy clients, Team, Blog; 'Get a free quote' in small caps with an arrow; 'Book a free call' coral button with navy text and a navy pin glyph. Past the hero the nav keeps its rule and the button compresses to glyph + label.
- 01 Hero (600px; 540px copy / 660px map, seam as a 1px navy rule with tick marks): eyebrow with a coral pin, 'One of Google's first nine certified agencies'; h1 'Put your cause on the map.'; sub naming the $10,000 a month and the 5% floor; 'Book a free call · 15 MIN' coral + 'Am I eligible? · 2 MIN' navy outline at equal 52px; one line of fine print; guarantee block with Amber Snow's portrait, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy' and 'Read the guarantee'. Map: contour field with stepped tints, grid numbers along the neatline and seam, furniture on a 32px inset from the seam and the right edge ('Sheet 01 · Reach survey' top-left, compass rose top-right, three-row legend bottom-left, 'As of 22 Sep 2026' on a white plate bottom-right, the two plates sharing one bottom edge), summit pin and card ('Your nonprofit · $10,000 / mo Google Ad Grant · Summit · grid 43 · 71'), three supporter pins with sample outcomes and 'SAMPLE · 12-mo outcome' tags, and the dashed 5% floor with its label straddling the line. Below 960px container width the map becomes the phone inset with the numbered key.
- 02 Trust (navy rule above, hairline below): row one = Letter from Google stamp, Michelle Hurtado named in mono, her quote in Source Serif italic; beside it the scale bar carrying 780+ / $48M+ / 100% as its divisions with 'Scale of operations · as of Sep 2026'; row two = 'Among 780+ clients' followed by UNCF, Scouting America, COPD Foundation, YWCA Chicago, Earthwatch, Solar Sister, AAU, JFCS as an index in small caps between hairlines.
- 03 The rules (Sheet 02, policy literacy): Requirement / What Google does if you miss it / What we do about it, covering 5% CTR, conversion tracking, single-word keywords, account structure, monthly login, geo-targeting, quality score; the CTR row carries the dashed floor swatch; sourced footnote to Google's policy page with date.
- 04 Eligibility checker (Sheet 03, rep-free exit): three questions (org type, country, working website) beside a small map that adds a contour per answer; a 'yes' drops a coral pin and offers the call; hospitals, schools and governments get an honest ineligible card quoting Google's definition.
- 05 Outcomes atlas (Sheet 04): a map of client outcomes plotted by city only for clients who consent to be named and placed, otherwise the sample-pin treatment; beneath it a hairline table with Organization, Vertical, Input, Outcome, Period, Source, filterable by vertical, each row with 'Open case file' and 'Forward to board (PDF)'.
- 06 What it costs: flat monthly fee stated plainly if leadership approves it, never a percentage of spend; the seven services (Ad Grant management, Website SEO, Content creation, VisitorEmail, Google Remarketing, Microsoft Advertising, Spanish ad creation) as a legend-style price list.
- 07 Certified by Google (contained navy band, not full-bleed): the one-of-nine inaugural certification, Google's conversion-value stat for certified-managed accounts with its source, Google Partner badge with clear space, Inc. 5000 x4; the compass rose in white at low opacity behind.
- 08 Your team, named: six to eight eye-level black-and-white rectangular portraits with role and 'Nonprofits I support'; copy stating who the prospect's named account lead will be.
- 09 Reporting, shown (Sheet 05): a real monthly report styled as a map sheet with a neatline and 'As of' readout: utilisation vs the $10,000 cap, CTR against the dashed floor, compliance ticks, mono REDACTED tags; beside it the one-sentence month signed by a named account lead with photo and date.
- 10 Guarantee band (navy): the $25 meet-the-CEO guarantee with Amber Snow named and pictured, 'Our guarantee is a person, not a policy', a single coral CTA.
- 11 FAQ: five plain-language questions in a hairline accordion (why pay for something free; will it raise money, answered honestly; who is on my account; what if we get suspended; how long to acquire), each with a dated source line where policy is cited.
- 12 Final CTA row: the hero action pair repeated verbatim plus 'See a real account report' opening a redacted PDF.
- 13 Footer: four columns, newsletter, address, socials, client login; 780+ used consistently; print stylesheet for the sheets and the guarantee page.
imagery: No illustration system and no stock photography; four image types. First, the map: a contour field generated by marching squares over a scalar terrain (one summit for the nonprofit, three knolls for supporters, two low shoulders), so contours merge and split the way real topography does; every loop is closed and carries a stepped hypsometric tint from #E6EDF1 to #F9FBFC; index contours every fourth line at 1.5px; the lowest contour dashed in navy as the 5% floor. Exported once per breakpoint as static inline SVG (about 10KB of path data on desktop, 6KB on the phone), with pins, cards, legend, compass, sheet label and readouts as DOM elements over it. Map furniture is drawn from real conventions: neatline, graticule ticks and two-digit grid numbers, a split-fill compass rose with a coral north point, a scale bar with alternating navy and white divisions. Grid references are neutral survey numbers, never latitude and longitude, so no location is implied until a client consents to be placed. Second, real photography of the 60+ team: black-and-white, eye-level, rectangular crops for the team section; small colour crops of Amber Snow and the named account leads (the mockups carry flat #C9D5DE placeholder frames with role='img' labels until the shoot). Third, real screens: the monthly report and the Ad Grants account view as map sheets with a neatline, an 'As of' readout, named client and month, and visible mono REDACTED tags instead of blur. Fourth, the client roll as typography: Source Serif small caps between hairlines, so it reads as an atlas index and needs no logo licensing. Iconography is one navy 1.5px stroke set built from the pin, the contour and the compass point; the pin appears in navy inside every primary button. Data viz: ground background, hairline gridlines, navy series one, contour-blue series two, coral reserved for the single highlighted point, a dashed navy horizontal line for the 5% CTR floor wherever CTR is charted, unit and period on every chart, sourced footnote beneath. Beneficiary photography appears only inside case files, with permission, never as homepage decoration.
motion: Static first, motion second, nothing depends on JavaScript. 1. Hero load (pure CSS, shipped in the mockup): the contours fade in from the summit outward, 50ms per level, so the terrain appears to rise around the pin; the summit pin drops 8px into place at 0.55s, the three supporter pins follow by distance at 0.78 / 0.88 / 0.98s, each card fades 120ms after its pin, then the floor label, sheet label, compass and legend settle by 1.3s. Copy is readable from frame one. 2. Phone: the inset's contours fade the same way and the numbered markers drop in order 1-2-3. 3. Buttons: hover lightens the coral to #EC7A55 (navy text stays above 4.5:1), pressed adds a navy border; the pin glyph does not move, the map is the only thing that moves. 4. Below the fold (optional GSAP + ScrollTrigger sprint, native scroll only, JS budget under 300kB): sections reveal with 12px translate and opacity; the eligibility map adds a contour per answer; the outcomes atlas pins drop as rows are filtered. 5. prefers-reduced-motion: every keyframe sits inside a no-preference media query, so reduced-motion users get the final state instantly with no animation at all. 6. Never: WebGL, kinetic type, parallax, autoplaying video, scroll-jacking, a spinning compass, gradients or drop shadows anywhere.
mobile: The 390px hero is a different composition, not the desktop squeezed. Nav (60px, navy rule beneath): 32px circular mark + 'Nonprofit Megaphone' at 15px, a 36px 'Book a call' coral button with navy text and pin glyph, and a 44px menu button with a visible focus ring. Hero (16px gutters): small caps eyebrow with its coral pin; h1 40px holding two lines ('Put your cause' / 'on the map.'); then the map as a 358 × 178 inset sheet with a 1px navy neatline, contours regenerated for the smaller field, the summit pin with its card ('Your nonprofit · $10,000 / mo Google Ad Grant'), three numbered navy markers, a 30px compass and an 'As of 22 Sep 2026' plate bottom-right; directly under it a three-row key (30px rows between hairlines) repeating the numbered markers with each outcome in 14px Source Sans 600 and a 'SAMPLE · 12 MO' mono tag, so every figure is readable text rather than a label crammed onto the map. Then a four-line sub at 16px, a full-width 52px 'Book a free call · 15 MIN' at 613px, a full-width 48px 'Am I eligible? · 2 MIN' outline button at 675px (both above the 760 fold; eligibility is a button, not a text link), and one centred line of fine print. One trust element follows: the Letter from Google stamp, the quote at 19px italic, Michelle Hurtado named, and '780+ nonprofits served · as of Sep 2026'. Below the fold the scale bar stacks as three cells, the rules table becomes a definition list, the outcomes atlas uses the inset-plus-key pattern, the price list keeps its legend form, and the team grid goes to two columns. Tap targets are 44px minimum; the page has no horizontal overflow at 390px.
a11y: Target WCAG 2.2 AA across the system. Contrast, measured on the actual backgrounds: #12203A ink on ground 13.7:1 and on white 16.2:1; #2E3D57 body on ground 9.2:1; #4E6079 muted labels on ground 5.4:1, on white 6.4:1, on the summit tint 6.1:1; navy text on the #E4643B button 4.78:1 and on the #EC7A55 hover 5.8:1 (white on coral was rejected at 3.4:1); coral is never used as text; coral pins carry a 0.8px navy hairline so they clear non-text contrast on the ground; contour lines are decorative and intentionally low-contrast at 1.8:1. Measured frames: desktop 1200 × 825 (nav 72 + hero 600 + trust 153) with no element outside the container and no horizontal scroll; phone 390 wide with the CTA at 613px and the eligibility button at 675px inside a 760px fold and no overflow. Type floor: 11px for mono readouts, tags and fine print; 12px legend rows; 13px small caps labels; 14px card titles and key rows; 15-18px for everything else; nothing is set below 11px. Diagram semantics: the map is a figure with aria-labelledby pointing to a visually hidden figcaption that states the argument (the summit and its grant, the three sample outcomes, the 5% floor, and that contours show reach not scale); the contour SVG, graticule numbers, compass, pin glyphs and the phone's numbered markers are aria-hidden; pin cards, the legend (role list), the floor label, the sheet label, the date readout and the phone key are real DOM text in reading order (summit first, then supporters by distance); portrait placeholders carry role='img' with a descriptive label. Focus: a 2px navy outline with 3px offset on every link and button via :focus-visible, visible on ground, white and coral. Motion: every animation is inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, so reduced-motion users get the final static state with zero keyframes; the load sequence runs once for 1.3s and nothing loops. Headings are sentence case; uppercase is reserved for mono readouts. Pointer targets 44px on touch; buttons 52px. Print stylesheet keeps the sheets and the guarantee legible in black on white.

heroCopy.eyebrow: One of Google's first nine certified agencies
heroCopy.headline: Put your cause on the map.
heroCopy.sub: Google gives eligible nonprofits $10,000 a month in search ads. We acquire the grant, keep it above Google's 5% click-through floor, and chart where your supporters are searching, month by month.

signatureMoments: The reach map: real marching-squares topography with the nonprofit at the summit, three supporter hills each pinned with a sample twelve-month outcome, the dashed 5% floor at the base and stepped hypsometric tints, all in one static inline SVG with every label as real text.

Map furniture as trust: the three trust figures set as the divisions of a scale bar captioned 'Scale of operations · as of Sep 2026', a compass rose whose north point is the only coral on the map that is not a pin, and the Letter from Google as an attestation stamp with the sender named.

The pin as the brand's verb: the same coral pin marks the summit, sits in navy inside every 'Book a free call' button, leads the eyebrow and keys the legend, so booking a call reads as putting yourself on the map.
Survey readouts: dates and grid references in DM Mono ('As of 22 Sep 2026', 'Summit · grid 43 · 71'), a quiet way of saying that every figure on this site carries a date.
The phone inset and key: the map folds to a 178px sheet with numbered navy markers and a three-row key beneath it, so the idea survives at 390px without shrinking a single label.
dependencies: Approve the coral-with-navy-text button: white on #E4643B fails AA at 3.4:1, so the choice is navy text on the current coral (shipped in the mockups) or a deeper coral for buttons only; the decision must precede the Webflow build.

Consent the three sample outcomes (2,300 new visitors a month; 300+ screenings a month; $38,000 a month in donations) as unattributed twelve-month figures from the published case files, or supply replacement figures the team prefers to show.

Decide whether real clients may be plotted by city on the outcomes atlas (Sheet 04); without consent the whole site uses the sample-pin treatment and neutral grid numbers, and no geography is claimed anywhere.
Photography half-day: small colour crops of Amber Snow and the named account leads, black-and-white eye-level portraits of the team; the mockups ship with labelled flat placeholder frames until then.

Webflow build of the map as a locked embed component (contours generated once per breakpoint from a small script, pins and cards as CMS fields with an outcome, a period and a sample flag) plus a style-guide page so editors cannot add colours, gradients or shadows.
risks: Coral on the cool ground is a low-contrast accent by design; if editors start using it for text, backgrounds or extra highlights the map loses its calm and the site fails AA. Lock coral to pins and button fills in the class set.

A map implies geography. The sample pins and grid numbers are deliberately abstract, but a skeptical reader could still read a pin as a place or a result as a promise; every outcome ships with a SAMPLE tag, a period and a case-file link, and real places appear only with consent.

Steel blue-gray plus navy can read cold or institutional if the human counterweights are cut: Amber Snow under the CTA, the named account lead, the signed monthly report and the team portraits are mandatory, not decorative.

The contour field is heavier than a flat illustration (about 10KB of path data on desktop, 6KB on the phone) and must ship as static inline SVG generated at build time, never as a runtime mapping library; a later editor asking for a real basemap would break both the budget and the idea.
references: Swisstopo and USGS topographic sheets (contour weight hierarchy, index contours, neatline and graticule conventions)
Ordnance Survey Explorer maps (legend design, small caps labels, one accent used sparingly)
Stamen Terrain and classic hypsometric atlases (elevation as flat tint steps rather than gradients)
Monocle (letterspaced small caps, calm authority, dated readouts)
Stripe (proof in the hero, numbers over adjectives, one action colour)
Field Notes and expedition equipment catalogues (expedition-grade product language and restraint)
